segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
254. There was a woman in it,
who owned two houses (or courtyards):
one was bought for three hundred dinars,
and the other for four hundred dinars.
And because of the plague of mice,
she rented {OCR?} one of them for seven zuzas,
and bought herself a cat with them.
And in the year 470,
470 of the Arabs,
which is the year 1389,
1389 of the Greeks,
(1078 of our Lord):
while Michael was feebly ruling the empire of the Romans, on account of the sickness of colic (or strangury) that befell him,
he sat inside the palace,
and the health of his body deteriorated,
and he was completely unable to meet anyone.
Then there rebelled against him a certain man whose name was Nikephoros Botaneiates,
who had formerly been a farmer,
and was promoted and ruled over the island of Cyprus,
then over Antioch.
Then he was removed from his governorship,
and was needy.
This man allied himself with an emir from the line of the Seljuks, whose name was Qutlumush son of Yabghu Arslan son of Seljuk,
who had fled from Sultan Alp Arslan and taken refuge in the Roman territory.
And they besieged Constantinople for four months,
and there was a great famine in it,
so that two loaves of bread were sold for a dinar,
and a hen for a dinar,
and fifteen eggs for a dinar.
And a plague also accompanied the famine.
One of those who carried the dead recounted,
who were bringing them into the crypt of the Great Church,
and from there, when the crypt was filled, they cast the corpses into the sea from the sea gate,
and in return for each dead person they took one fols (small coin):
that they took one hundred and sixty thousand fulus during these four months.
The chronicler says:
"Such a great number is incredible,
but I wrote as I heard."
And when the patriarch and the magnates saw
that Michael was unable to repel the oppressors,
they opened the gates
and surrendered the city to Nikephoros.
And when he entered it,
Michael came out on foot, carrying the crown in his hand, and said to him:
"Take it, and withhold the sword from the people;
and if you had asked it of me, I would have given it without war."
And he commanded him to be tonsured.
And when he became a monk
and refrained from the eating of meat,
he was healed of his illness,
and in monasticism he ended his life.
